write-batch-spec-yaml-file: 1. Write a batch spec YAML file
batch-spec-description: The batch spec ( <0>syntax reference</0> ) describes what the batch change does. You'll provide it when previewing, creating, and updating batch changes. We recommend committing it to source control.
preview-batch-change-sourcegraph-cli: 2. Preview the batch change with Sourcegraph CLI
use-sourcegraph-cli-preview: Use the <0>Sourcegraph CLI (src)</0>  to preview the commits and changesets that your batch change will make:
follow-url-for-preview: Follow the URL printed in your terminal to see the preview and (when you're ready) create the batch change.
create-batch-change-steps: Follow these steps to create a Batch Change. Need help? View the <0>documentation.</0>
license-changeset-limit: Your license only allows for {{maxUnlicensedChangesets}} changesets per batch change
batch-spec-execution-warning: You can execute this batch spec and see how it operates, but if more than {{maxUnlicensedChangesets}} changesets are generated, you won't be able to apply the batch change and actually publish the changesets to the code host.
batch-change-name-description: Give it a short, descriptive name to reference the batch change on Sourcegraph. Do not include confidential information. <0>Only letters, numbers, _, and - are allowed.</0>
